static_call_trace.behavior: Fixture uses a simple ReadOwner GenServer and real Admission gate. Parser/service configuration and gate acquisition occur before timing. The test swaps in HTTP2.Transport with the fake owner, sets a 30 ms deadline, suspends owner, then starts timing. No HTTP listener, connection, peer, or upstream request is created by this fixture.

read_req_body enters read_body, checks remaining absolute deadline, computes body reservation, and calls update_body before transport dispatch. The measured interval therefore includes admission reservation and error cleanup as well as Continue.

update_body_retention passes Lifecycle.remaining(deadline) to Admission.update/4, whose GenServer.call is bounded by that remaining value. Admission update adjusts bytes and calls sample -> Telemetry.emit -> telemetry.execute before replying. telemetry is unchanged. A timeout is mapped to {:error, :timeout}.

Exchange dispatches to HTTP2.Transport.read_body_step. maybe_continue sets expect_sent and calls operation(exchange, :read_continue) before the H2 body-read operation. If the earlier deadline check or admission update expires, this branch need not be reached; the CI log has no phase-level trace proving which timeout branch executed.

The specific :read_continue branch computes min(request deadline, now + write_timeout) and GenServer.call(fake_suspended_owner, {:h2_operation, id, token, {:write, deadline, {:head, 100, [], false}}}, remaining). The suspended owner cannot reply. The timeout is caught as {:error, :timeout}. This branch does not use the generic operation/2 remaining + 100 allowance at line 87.

body_error releases adapter retention before returning {:error, :timeout}. At expired deadline, update_body_retention returns timeout immediately; defer_body_retention uses gen_server.send_request and receive_response(request, 0). This introduces no intentional blocking cleanup grace period.

now/deadline/remaining use monotonic milliseconds. Remaining is clamped at zero. The API passes a finite remaining timeout; this does not prove the caller will be scheduled to resume within the elapsed test threshold.
